Disease Outbreak Disrupts Vietnam's Industrial Intermediate Prod Sector

A disease outbreak at several industrial intermediate product manufacturing sites in Vietnam has led to widespread workforce shortages and significant operational disruptions, according to industry sources. The outbreak, identified as a cluster of acute respiratory infections, was first reported last week at a major plant operated by Delta Materials Ltd. in Binh Duong province, before cases emerged at neighboring facilities.

"Approximately 30% of our workforce is currently on medical leave," said Le Hoang Minh, human resources manager at Delta Materials. "We have temporarily scaled down production, and some assembly lines are operating at just 50% capacity." The Vietnam Association of Industrial Intermediate Producers (VAIIP) estimates that overall sector output has dropped by at least 25% since the first cases were detected.

Local health authorities have implemented screening and containment measures at affected sites, including temporary closures of common areas and staggered shifts to reduce contact among employees. However, VAIIP secretary-general Tran Thi Lan warned that "ongoing transmission risks mean further slowdowns may be necessary."

The intermediate product sector, which supplies components such as industrial adhesives, resins, and specialty coatings for domestic and export markets, plays a critical role in Vietnam’s manufacturing value chain. "Delays in component deliveries are already being reported by several of our clients," said a spokesperson for Hoang Anh Supply Corp., another affected manufacturer.

Analysts say the full impact on the sector will depend on how quickly the outbreak is contained. "Prolonged absenteeism could lead to more severe supply chain bottlenecks," said Nguyen Quoc Phong, an industrial analyst at Saigon Research Partners. As of Friday, there was no official timeline for a return to normal operations.
